title: Axillary Nerve Injury
subtitle: Peripheral nerve injury of the upper limb
overview: Damage to the axillary nerve, which arises from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C5-C6). Often caused by shoulder dislocation or fracture of the humeral surgical neck.
presentation:
• Weakness in shoulder abduction (deltoid muscle).
  • Sensory loss over the lateral aspect of the shoulder (regimental badge area).
diagnosticScans: Electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies. MRI of the shoulder to rule out structural damage or compression.
management: Conservative treatment including physical therapy. Surgical exploration or nerve grafting if no recovery is observed within 3-6 months.

title: Multiple Sclerosis
subtitle: Chronic demyelinating disease of the CNS
overview: An autoimmune, inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Characterized by lesions separated in time and space.
presentation:
• Optic neuritis (painful vision loss).
  • Sensory disturbances, fatigue, spasticity, and gait imbalance.
  • Lhermitte's sign (electric shock sensation down the spine with neck flexion).
diagnosticScans: MRI of brain and spine showing demyelinating plaques (McDonald criteria). Lumbar puncture showing oligoclonal bands in CSF.
management: Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) to reduce relapses and slow disability progression. Corticosteroids for acute relapses.
